A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphDO study and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original LLM experiments across six graph tasks, including accuracy results in Tables 1–2, analyses in Figures 3–7, and response case studies in Appendix D.

after.justification: v6 reports original graph-task evaluations, numerical accuracy results, order and model comparisons, and model-response case studies in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The adjacency encoding, BFS/DFS traversal procedures, PR/PPR ordering, and task-specific personalization vectors in Section 3 and Appendix A.2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six GraphDO tasks: five synthetic graph-reasoning tasks and node classification on CORA, Citeseer, and Pubmed. The sampling scenarios and shortest/longest-path ordering scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Random, BFS, DFS, PR, and PPR. The shortest/longest-path comparison in Figure 6 and Random/BFS/DFS comparisons across models in Figure 7 also retain identical comparator membership.

E3.justification: The six LLMs, five prompt styles, zero decoding temperature, accuracy metric, graph generation and sampling settings, and response-parsing procedures remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices A–C.

E4.justification: The order-sensitivity analysis in Figure 4, answer-overlap experiment in Figure 6, model comparison in Figure 7, and case analyses in Appendix D and Tables 4–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the statement that node-classification experiments were repeated three times. Figure 4 retains the same variance across description orders; no run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and appendix response cases are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains average connectivity accuracies of 89.43% for BFS and 78.36% for Random. The embedded figure content is identical.

T1.justification: The graph/task definitions, Equations (1)–(3), PR/PPR formulas, Figure 4 variance definition, and Appendix A.2 personalization formulas are mathematically unchanged. Differences are typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about novelty, benefits of ordered graph descriptions, task-dependent effects, and the GraphDO dataset contribution.

C2.justification: The attention-bias hypothesis, explanations of task/order differences and answer overlap, and limitations concerning graph-structure coverage and the absence of rigorous theoretical explanation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5's abstract supplies a code-availability statement and GraphDO repository link; v6 removes both without replacement elsewhere. Implementation and data-generation details remain unchanged. This establishes removal of access information, not unavailability of the repository itself.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including the positioning relative to graph encoding, prompting, and LLM-reasoning research.

P1.justification: The abstract loses its final code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date text changes. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There is limited text reflow on the opening pages and spacing changes within tables, including appendix Tables 4–5. Figures, table organization, axes, legends, and substantive captions are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 removes the paper's only explicit code-access statement and link, reducing guidance for locating the implementation. The scientific evidence, explanations, and limitations are unchanged; the minor typesetting changes do not offset this limited loss of reproducibility information.
